methodologyNotes: Covers standalone desktop KVM (keyboard-video-mouse) switches and USB-C KVM docking switches that let one keyboard, monitor set, and mouse control two or more computers, sold at a published US price. Excludes IP/remote KVM-over-IP appliances, rackmount enterprise matrix switches, and monitors with a built-in KVM feature. Price is US MSRP or typical street price in USD. portCount is the number of source computers the switch connects (count). displayHeads is the number of monitors driven per computer (1 = single-head, 2 = dual-head; count). videoInterface is the primary console video connector, an enum of HDMI, DisplayPort, USB-C, or Mixed (when inputs/outputs combine types). maxResolution is the highest supported resolution and refresh as pixels@Hz (e.g. 3840x2160@60), NOT interpolated. maxRefreshAt4kHz is the maximum refresh rate at 4K UHD (3840x2160) in Hz; null if the switch does not reach 4K. usbHubStandard is the shared peripheral USB generation, an enum of USB 2.0, USB 3.0 (5 Gbps), or USB 3.2 (10 Gbps). usbPortCount is the count of shared USB peripheral ports exposed to the connected computers (count). edidEmulation is a boolean: true if the switch emulates/retains EDID so windows do not rearrange on switch. audioSupport is a boolean: true if it has dedicated analog 3.5mm audio jacks. powerDeliveryWatts is the maximum USB-C Power Delivery to a connected laptop in watts; null if the switch does not charge hosts over USB-C. switchingMethods lists the supported input-switch controls as a slash-delimited enum drawn from button, hotkey, remote, mouse.
